options.text: A root of all kinds of evil

mc.good: Correct. The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.
mc.bad: Look again: Paul says the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.

quiz.reflectPrompt: Have you seen how the love of money can be dangerous in your life or others'? How can you use money in ways that bring praise to God?

lessons.prayer: Lord, guard my heart from loving money. Help me be content, put my hope in you, and give generously to those in need. Amen.

lessons.title: Live 9: Marriage and family
teaching: Many people carry pain from broken homes and have lost hope for their own future marriage. But there is fresh hope in God's plan. Out of love for Christ, husbands and wives are to follow one another's lead, treating each other with the same love and respect they give the Lord, working as a loving team rather than as competitors.

The word 'head' means source of strength and protection, not boss; husbands are to serve and sacrifice for their wives as Christ did for the church. Children are to obey and honour their parents, and parents are to keep pointing their children to God through their own example. Such marriages and families are a blessing to each other, to God and to the world.
lessons.keyIdea: Husbands, love your wives just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her.
lessons.reflectionScript: Picture a triangle with God at the top and a husband and wife at the two lower corners. As each one moves closer to God, they move closer to each other. That is the secret of a strong marriage, and the secret of a strong family too. Even now, whatever your home has been like, you can begin drawing closer to God and learning to love, respect and serve the people around you.

mc.question: How are husbands told to treat their wives?

options.text: To love them as Christ loved the church

mc.good: Correct. Husbands are to love their wives as Christ loved the church and gave himself for her.
mc.bad: Look again: husbands are to love their wives sacrificially, as Christ loved the church.

quiz.reflectPrompt: What experiences have you had of others' marriages? If you hope to marry one day, how can you start preparing now, and how can you honour God in your family today?

lessons.prayer: Lord, thank you for your good plan for marriage and family. Prepare me now to love, respect and serve, and help me honour my family today. Amen.

lessons.title: Live 10: Emotional pain
teaching: Emotional pain is real, and if it is not dealt with it becomes baggage that weighs us down and steals our hope. It comes from being hurt or used, from shattered dreams, mistakes and tough times. Christ wants us to find him in our pain so that we become pioneers of our future rather than prisoners of our past.

Paul wrote these words from prison and teaches us to see all pain as an opportunity to draw closer to God, not to face hardship alone, to trust God's resurrection power to help us overcome, to forget what is behind by forgiving those who hurt us, and to press on toward what lies ahead.
lessons.keyIdea: Forget what is behind and press on toward the goal. Bitterness is like drinking poison and hoping the other person will die.
lessons.reflectionScript: Bitterness is like drinking poison and hoping the other person will die; it only harms us. Bring to mind someone who has hurt you. Forgiveness is not saying it did not matter; it is a choice to set yourself free. Picture yourself handing that pain to God, refusing to carry it anymore, and turning to face the future he is opening in front of you. What dream is he calling you toward?

mc.question: What is the one thing Paul says he does?

options.text: Forgets what is behind and presses toward the goal
Gives up when life is hard

mc.good: Correct. Paul forgets what is behind and strains toward what is ahead.
mc.bad: Look again: Paul forgets what is behind and presses on toward the goal.

quiz.reflectPrompt: What emotional pain are you struggling with? How can you deal with it in a God-pleasing way, and what dreams has God put in your heart for the future?

lessons.prayer: Lord, thank you that in you I am not a prisoner of my past. Help me forgive those who hurt me and press on toward the future you have for me. Amen.

lessons.title: Change 1: Bringing about change
teaching: We are on this planet to reflect Christ's character and do God's will. If Christ is the hope of the world, then God's people are the messengers of that hope, on a mission to bring change starting with the people around us.

Salt only works when it leaves the shaker and touches the food, so God gives each of us a mission field: our family, community and those we study or work with. A life 'salty' with passion for God makes others thirst for him. Light is meant to be seen, not hidden; following Jesus is personal but not private. Some will hate the light, but others will see our good deeds and give glory to God.
lessons.keyIdea: Let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven.
lessons.reflectionScript: Salt stuck in the shaker changes nothing; it has to touch the food. Light hidden under a bowl gives no help. Picture the people God has already placed around you, your family, classmates, workmates, as your mission field. You do not need a stage. You need a life that quietly makes others thirsty for God. What would it look like to let your light shine there this week?

mc.question: What does Jesus call his followers in this passage?

options.text: The salt of the earth and the light of the world

mc.good: Correct. Jesus calls his followers the salt of the earth and the light of the world.
mc.bad: Look again: Jesus calls his followers salt and light.

quiz.reflectPrompt: How do you feel about being salt and light? How would it change your lifestyle if you began to see the people around you as your mission field?

lessons.prayer: Lord, make me salt and light where you have placed me. Let my life make others thirst for you and give glory to your name. Amen.

lessons.title: Change 2: Telling your story
teaching: A young woman named Susan trusted Christ for the first time and was immediately encouraged by a text from a stranger who had felt led to message an unknown number, hers. You too have a story of God's goodness to tell.

Paul told his God-story to unbelievers, and we can learn from him: describe a little about your life before you trusted Christ, explain the events that led to you becoming a follower of Jesus, and tell how your life has changed since. Your experience does not need to be dramatic. If God has forgiven you, freed you, given you peace or answered prayer, simply share it, and if it is real, people will be impacted.
lessons.keyIdea: You are a witness of what God has done for you. Portray Jesus as the hero of your story, and people will move closer to trusting him.
lessons.reflectionScript: Think back over your own journey with God. What was life like before you knew him? What happened that began to change things? What is different now? You do not need a dramatic testimony, only a true one. Picture yourself simply telling a friend one honest thing God has done for you. That small story could be the crack of light through which someone else finds him.

mc.question: How did Paul share his story with the crowd?

options.text: By telling about his life before, how he met Christ, and how he changed

mc.good: Correct. Paul told about his old life, his conversion, and the change afterward.
mc.bad: Look again: Paul told his story in three parts, his life before, his encounter with Christ, and how he changed.

quiz.reflectPrompt: What was your life like before, what happened to change it, and what is your life like now? Ask God for an opportunity to share your story.

lessons.prayer: Lord, thank you for what you have done in my life. Give me courage and opportunities to tell my story, always making you the hero. Amen.

lessons.title: Change 3: Spreading the gospel
teaching: If you had a cure for a deadly disease, you would not keep it to yourself; the gospel is even better news. This passage gives five truths: we are all sinners separated from God and needing salvation, our salvation was achieved by Christ's death, it unites us to Christ now and forever.

Our salvation is by grace, not by works, so our good deeds do not qualify us and our bad deeds do not disqualify us; we simply receive God's grace by faith. And salvation leads to a changed life, as God transforms us and uses us to change the world. These simple truths have the power to change people's lives forever.
lessons.keyIdea: It is by grace you have been saved, through faith; it is God's gift, not the result of works, so no one can boast.
lessons.reflectionScript: Hold this in your mind: your good deeds could never earn your salvation, and your worst deeds cannot cancel it out. It is a gift, received by faith. Now think of the people around you who have never truly heard that. Picture their faces. Someone told you this good news, or you would still be in the dark. Who is God nudging you to tell? Ask him to open the door.

mc.question: According to this passage, how are we saved?

options.text: By grace through faith, as God's gift
By being born into the right family

mc.good: Correct. We are saved by grace through faith; it is the gift of God, not by works.
mc.bad: Look again: we are saved by grace through faith, as God's gift, not by works.

quiz.reflectPrompt: Write these five truths in your own words and try to memorise them. Who would you like to share them with? Pray for those people by name.

lessons.prayer: Lord, thank you for saving me by grace, not because I earned it. Help me share this good news clearly with people who need to hear it. Amen.

lessons.title: Change 4: Using your gifts
teaching: Your body works best when every part does its unique job; if your legs or eyes stopped working one morning, the whole body would suffer. The Church is like a body, and you have a special function that no one else has, given to build up the whole body and reach the world.

Common spiritual gifts include sensing what God is saying, practical service, teaching, encouraging, giving, leadership and helping the hurting. We are to use these gifts humbly, appreciating everyone since each person has at least one gift, developing our skills through practice, and serving as much as we can rather than focusing on what we cannot do.
lessons.keyIdea: Each of us has different gifts given by God's grace. Fan them into flame and use them faithfully to serve others.
lessons.reflectionScript: Every gift starts out undeveloped, like a small spark before it becomes a fire. Maybe you are unsure what yours even is. Think about what you enjoy, what others thank you for, what needs stir you to act. Picture that spark being fanned into flame as you practise and serve. God gave you your gift on purpose. The Church, the body, is not complete without your part.

mc.question: What attitude does Paul warn against when using our gifts?

options.text: Being proud or thinking of ourselves too highly

mc.good: Correct. Paul warns us not to be proud but to think of ourselves with sober judgment.
mc.bad: Look again: Paul warns against pride and calls us to think of ourselves humbly.

quiz.reflectPrompt: Looking at the list of gifts, what do you think your gift or gifts may be? How can you, with the Spirit's help, develop them for God's glory and others' good?

lessons.prayer: Lord, thank you for the gifts you have given me. Keep me humble, and help me develop and use them faithfully to serve others. Amen.

lessons.title: Change 5: Serving others
teaching: In our world the greatest person is usually the one with the most people serving them, but in God's kingdom the greatest is the one who serves others. Jesus turns everything upside down, making the last first.

We serve others because it is love in action, because in God's kingdom we exist for others, because God blesses us when we serve, and because Jesus said it is more blessed to give than to receive. Remembering who we are in Christ frees us to humble ourselves and find practical, even lowly, ways to serve, just as Jesus washed his disciples' feet.
lessons.keyIdea: Jesus washed his disciples' feet and told us to do the same. Don't seek to be served, but to serve.
lessons.reflectionScript: Picture the Lord of the universe kneeling on the floor with a towel and basin, washing the dirty feet of his friends. This is greatness in God's kingdom, not being served, but serving. Where has God placed you, at home, at school, at work? Imagine one humble, practical act of service you could offer someone there. Then let Jesus' example give you the freedom to do it.

mc.question: What did Jesus do to show his love and set an example for his disciples?
mc.good: Correct. Jesus washed his disciples' feet as an example of humble service.
mc.bad: Look again: Jesus washed his disciples' feet and told them to serve one another.

quiz.reflectPrompt: How do you feel about serving others, and what holds you back? In what practical ways can you become more of a servant this week?

lessons.prayer: Lord Jesus, you knelt to wash feet. Free me from pride and give me a servant's heart to serve others in practical, humble ways. Amen.

lessons.title: Change 6: Helping the hurting
teaching: A man throwing stranded starfish back into the sea one at a time realised he could not save them all, but he could make a difference for this one, and this one, and that one. The pain and injustice around us can overwhelm us, but God calls us to do what we can.

In the parable, the religious people passed by while the despised Samaritan lovingly did what he could. Following Jesus means loving those around us, especially the hurting, doing what we can and encouraging others to join in. Being a Christian is not only about loving God; it is about loving people too, and serving broken people draws us closer to the God who loves them.
lessons.keyIdea: Love your neighbour as yourself. Whatever we do for the least of these, we do for Jesus himself.
lessons.reflectionScript: Imagine walking past someone in real need, the way the busy and religious did in the story. Now imagine being the one who stops, kneels, and helps, even at a cost. Jesus said that whatever we do for the least of these, we do for him. Who is the wounded person on your road right now? You may not be able to help everyone, but you can help this one.

mc.question: Who stopped to help the wounded man in the parable?
mc.good: Correct. It was the Samaritan, looked down on by others, who stopped and helped.
mc.bad: Look again: the priest and Levite passed by, but the Samaritan stopped to help.

quiz.reflectPrompt: How do you feel about being more compassionate toward hurting people, and what holds you back? Where can you start helping others wisely?

lessons.prayer: Lord, give me eyes to see the hurting and a heart to help. Let me love my neighbour as myself and serve you by serving them. Amen.

lessons.title: Change 7: Becoming empowered
teaching: An electric guitar unplugged can barely be heard, but plugged into an amplifier it can fill a stadium. God wants to plug our small lives into the power of his Spirit so our impact is far greater than anything we could do in our own cleverness or determination.

God promises us the gift of the Holy Spirit. When we are saved we are born of the Spirit, but God also wants to fill us with the Spirit so we experience his presence, power and boldness to be witnesses. Jesus tells us to come thirsting and ask in simple trust to be filled, and to keep being filled every day by giving the Spirit total control of our lives.
lessons.keyIdea: You will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you, and you will be Jesus' witnesses.
lessons.reflectionScript: Picture an electric guitar played without being plugged in, its sound thin and faint. Then imagine it connected to a powerful amplifier, filling a whole stadium. That is the difference the Holy Spirit makes. In your own strength you can only do so much. Come thirsty, like a dry field before rain, and ask God to fill you. Then imagine being empowered to make a difference far beyond yourself.

mc.question: What did Jesus promise his followers before returning to heaven?

options.text: Power through the coming of the Holy Spirit

mc.good: Correct. Jesus promised they would receive power when the Holy Spirit came on them.
mc.bad: Look again: Jesus promised power through the Holy Spirit so they could be his witnesses.

quiz.reflectPrompt: Can you think of times when you sensed the Spirit's presence or use in your life? Find time alone today to ask Jesus to fill you with his Spirit.

lessons.prayer: Jesus, I come thirsting to you. Fill me with your Holy Spirit and give me power and boldness to be your witness. Amen.

lessons.title: Change 8: Making peace
teaching: A man once built a fence to keep out a neighbour he disliked, then, when God told him to make peace, he tore it down and used the wood to build a path to the neighbour's door. Our world is hurting because of the fences of hostility, prejudice and superiority we build; God calls us to build paths instead.

When we follow Jesus we are no longer identified mainly by class, culture, race or gender, but by our new identity in God as his loved and chosen people. We seek peace by getting rid of anger and hate, becoming compassionate, kind, humble, patient, forgiving and loving, and above all letting God's love bind us together in unity. Change must start with the Church.
lessons.keyIdea: Over all these virtues put on love, which binds them all together in perfect unity. Become a peacemaker.
lessons.reflectionScript: Picture a fence someone built between two homes, and then imagine that same wood taken down and laid out as a path from one door to the other. Think of a relationship in your life marked by tension, prejudice or hurt. What would it look like to build a path instead of a wall? Ask God to clothe you with compassion, patience and love, and to make you a bridge of peace.

mc.question: According to Paul, what binds all the virtues together in unity?
mc.good: Correct. Over all the virtues we are to put on love, which binds everything together in unity.
mc.bad: Look again: Paul says love binds all the virtues together in perfect unity.

quiz.reflectPrompt: How have you experienced prejudice, division or hostility in your world? What changes must happen in your heart, and where can you start being a peacemaker?

lessons.prayer: Lord, tear down the fences of hostility and prejudice in my heart. Clothe me with love and make me a peacemaker in your name. Amen.

lessons.title: Change 9: Leading others
teaching: Jesus chose twelve unimpressive, ordinary men to be the first Christian leaders, and young Timothy was chosen to oversee a whole church. Throughout history, when God wants to do something, he often taps an ordinary person on the shoulder. A leader is simply an influencer.

Leaders in God's kingdom are very different from leaders in the world. They have experienced Christ personally, care for people's spiritual well-being, take responsibility, serve rather than seek money or fame, lead by example rather than by control, draw people to Christ rather than to themselves, follow other leaders well, and stay humble, keeping their eyes on Jesus the Chief Shepherd.
lessons.keyIdea: Be shepherds of God's flock, serving eagerly and leading by example, not lording it over others.
lessons.reflectionScript: Imagine God quietly tapping you on the shoulder and saying, I need you to do something for me. Leadership in his kingdom is not about titles or control; it is about serving, caring, and setting an example. Maybe there is an opportunity or responsibility you have been running from. Picture yourself stepping into it, not proudly, but humbly, eyes fixed on Jesus, ready to help others rise.

mc.question: How does Peter say leaders should serve God's flock?

options.text: Willingly and eagerly, as examples, not for money

mc.good: Correct. Leaders are to serve willingly and eagerly, as examples, not for dishonest gain.
mc.bad: Look again: leaders serve willingly and eagerly, as examples, not for money or control.

quiz.reflectPrompt: How do you feel about being a spiritual leader or influencer for Christ? What can you do to become a better influencer of others?

lessons.prayer: Lord, you raise up ordinary people to lead. Make me a humble servant-leader who influences others toward you, keeping my eyes on you, the Chief Shepherd. Amen.

lessons.title: Change 10: Praying more
teaching: A father could easily move a couch alone, but he asked his little son to help, and the boy felt special sharing the task. God could change the world by himself, but he lovingly lets his children help him, and one major way we work with him is through prayer.

Jesus teaches us to pray with compassion for others' needs, with boldness, with perseverance, keeping on asking, seeking and knocking without giving up, and with trust in a good and powerful Father. We also pray for the help of the Spirit, and when what we ask matches what God wants, he changes situations and hearts.
lessons.keyIdea: Ask and it will be given; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened. Prayer is how we partner with God.
lessons.reflectionScript: Imagine a small child helping a parent lift something far too heavy for them alone. The parent carries almost all the weight, but the child feels honoured to share the task. That is prayer. God does the real work, yet he invites you to partner with him. Bring to mind one person or situation you long to see change. Picture yourself bringing it to your Father again and again, refusing to give up.

mc.question: What does Jesus teach about asking in prayer?

options.text: Keep asking, seeking and knocking, and don't give up
Give up if there is no quick answer

mc.good: Correct. Jesus urges us to keep asking, seeking and knocking, with persistence and trust.
mc.bad: Look again: Jesus says to keep asking, seeking and knocking, and not give up.

quiz.reflectPrompt: Can you name three ways you have experienced God answering your prayers? Who and what are some of the people and situations you are praying for now?

lessons.prayer: Father, thank you that you invite me to work with you through prayer. Give me compassion, boldness and persistence, and help me never give up. Amen.
